I have a small plot of sorghum, only 0.08 hectares, and it is intercropped with beans. I will go to the cooperative and try to get some DAP and urea fertilizer, though the supply is often late and not enough, so I can only put a small amount on this plot. I will also spread manure from my livestock because the soil needs whatever help it can get, and I have always saved my own sorghum seed from last year to plant. I do not have money for chemicals or irrigation, so my family will do all the work ourselves—weeding, harvesting, and threshing—since the plot is small enough to manage.
